title: SCHC 5.6: tombstone/admission-floor 256-per-direction bound + oldest-by-terminal-time eviction not implemented
description: spec/03-adaptation.md 5.6: 'Tombstone and admission-floor tables MUST be bounded to at most 256 entries per direction. On overflow, implementations MUST evict the oldest tombstone by terminal-time.' Classification: divergent (mechanism absent; boundedness achieved differently). Evidence: Rust FragmentationPolicyEntry stores [Option<TerminalTombstone>; 2] per peer per direction (rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs:196-197), reclaimed by 60s expiry (fragment.rs:1220-1247) and generation wipe — no 256 cap, no terminal-time eviction anywhere (rg clean). Python: no 256 cap; rejection-table overflow fails closed by advancing the floor and silently dropping (python/src/lichen/schc/reassembly.py:636-638, 662-664). Practical impact low: structural bounds are stricter (production Rust <=16 tombstones total). Suggested placement: either implement the literal bound+eviction or amend spec 5.6 to name the structural-bounds alternative. Filed from spec-coverage sweep 2026-08-31 (R-03-044).
